record.context_brief: Defect e ﬀect and independent systems of equations
record.original_question: Does there exist an independent system of three equations in three variables having a non-periodic solution?

evidence.quote: Does an independent system of three equations in three variables with a non-period solution exists?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and $\Sigma^+$ the free semigroup of nonempty words over $\Sigma$. Let $\Xi=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ be a set of three unknowns. A (constant-free) word equation in the unknowns $\Xi$ is a pair $(u,v)\in\Xi^+\times\Xi^+$, written $u=v$. A solution is a morphism $h:\Xi^+\to\Sigma^+$ with $h(u)=h(v)$; the solution is called periodic if there exists $w\in\Sigma^+$ such that $h(x_i)\in w^+$ for all $i=1,2,3$, and non-periodic otherwise.

A system $E=\{u_1=v_1,\ldots,u_k=v_k\}$ of word equations is called independent if no proper subsystem of $E$ has the same set of solutions as $E$ (equivalently, $E$ is not equivalent to any of its proper subsystems).

Question: Does there exist an independent system of three word equations in the three unknowns $x_1,x_2,x_3$ that admits a non-periodic solution $h:\Xi^+\to\Sigma^+$?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers on independent systems of three-unknown constant-free word equations (e.g., the "From Ehrenfeucht to Eighteen" line of work and subsequent papers on solution sets of three-variable word equations) report only upper bounds — at most 18 in general, at most 17 if a non-periodic solution exists — and explicitly state the conjecture that the maximal size is a small constant, with no known construction realizing three independent equations sharing a non-periodic solution. No solution to the existence question has been reported, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Independent Systems of Word Equations: From Ehrenfeucht to Eighteen
status_evidence.snippet: The maximal size of an independent system of three-variable equations is at most 18, and at most 17 if it has a non-periodic solution; the conjectured bound is a small constant.
status_evidence.claim: The exact maximal size of an independent system of three-variable constant-free word equations (in particular with a non-periodic solution) is unresolved; only upper bounds are known.

status_evidence.title: On the Solution Sets of Three-Variable Word Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses non-periodic solutions of systems of three-variable word equations and parametric descriptions, citing the open status of bounds on independent systems.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to treat bounds on independent three-variable systems with non-periodic solutions as an open question.
